source_text: Si fideliter invitas homines ad studium continentiae, fateris ergo ita virtutem pudicitiae a volentibus posse servari, ut sit, quicumque voluerit, corpore sanctus et spiritu Ob hoc a me christiani temporis continentiam fuisse laudatam, non ut ad virginitatem incenderentur homines, sed ut bonum nuptiarum quod a Deo institutum est damnaretur
pass_a_gloss: If fideliter invitas human-beings to studium continentiae, fateris therefore so virtue of-modesty from volentibus to-be-able servari, so-that/as may-be, quicumque voluerit, in-the-body holy and spiritu on-account-of this from me Christians of-time continentiam to-have-been laudatam, not so-that/as to virginitatem incenderentur human-beings, but so-that/as good of-marriages that/which from to-God institutum is damnaretur.

lemmas.lexica: LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good

pass_b_english: You praised continence in the Christian age not to kindle people toward virginity, but to condemn the good of marriage established by God.

If you sincerely invite people to pursue continence, then you acknowledge that those who will it can maintain chastity’s virtue, so that whoever wishes may be holy in body and spirit (compare 1 Corinthians 7:34).

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
